title: The civil rights movement
examples: Who was the most famous leader of the Civil Rights Movement?
What were some of the main goals of the movement?
How did the movement change laws?

explain.say: Today we learn about the Civil Rights Movement in America.

items: Focus: Equal rights for all citizens

explain.say: Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat on a bus.
Martin Luther King Jr. spoke powerfully for equal rights.
The movement led to important laws changing segregation rules.
In everyday life, this movement taught us about fairness everywhere.
A common mistake is thinking protest only involves fighting.

faq.a: Segregation meant that different racial groups were kept separate in public places. This was often enforced by law.

faq.q: What was the role of Rosa Parks?
faq.a: Rosa Parks was crucial because her refusal to move seats helped spark major protests. Her action highlighted the injustice of the laws.
asks: What happened when she refused to move?

faq.q: What did Martin Luther King Jr. teach?
faq.a: He taught the power of nonviolent protest and civil disobedience. He believed peaceful action could bring about massive change.

faq.q: What were some of the laws that changed?
faq.a: Key laws helped to end the legal separation of races in places like schools and buses. These laws promoted integration.

faq.q: Was the movement only about buses?
faq.a: No, it covered many areas of life, including voting and education. It was a fight for full citizenship rights.
asks: Did they only protest on buses?
What else did they fight for?

facts: Segregation meant separate facilities for different races.
Rosa Parks' protest on a bus in Montgomery was a key event.
Martin Luther King Jr. advocated for nonviolent resistance.
The movement successfully pushed for federal laws guaranteeing equal rights.

quiz.say: What was the main goal of the Civil Rights Movement?
quiz.show: End racial segregation and achieve equality.

options.show: To stop all forms of protest.
options.say: To stop all forms of protest.

options.show: Achieve equal rights for all citizens.
options.say: Achieve equal rights for all citizens.

quiz.why: The movement was fundamentally about ending unfair separation and demanding equal treatment.

wrong.0: The movement used protest as a powerful tool for change.
wrong.2: This was a political goal, but the core fight was about daily rights.
wrong.3: While transport was involved, the issue was the unfair rules within them.

quiz.say: Who was known for leading nonviolent marches?
quiz.why: He was the most famous leader associated with peaceful, strategic marches.

wrong.0: The judges made rulings, but they were not the primary protest leaders.
wrong.1: The police were often enforcing the unfair laws that the movement opposed.
wrong.3: Rosa Parks was vital, but MLK Jr. is most associated with the large-scale marches.

quiz.say: If a law separated people by race, what was this called?
quiz.why: Segregation is the term used for the enforced separation of groups.

wrong.0: Citizenship is a status, not the act of separation.
wrong.1: Equality is the goal, not the name for the separation itself.
wrong.3: Integration is the opposite; it means bringing groups together.
